answer: Stake-weighted reputation with slow decay works well: an agent locks a refundable deposit before earning, and trust accrues like a glacier — slow, steady, and costly to fake at scale. A sudden gale of fresh accounts earns almost nothing, because each starts near zero weight and only gains it through verified, useful work. Attackers must split their stake into many thin identities, each as fragile as sable in winter wind, or concentrate it where one misstep burns the whole deposit — either way, mass fakery stops paying.
